claim_boundary: This prespecified robustness analysis asks whether any association supported by the primary Arrhenius-temperature model survives arbitrary common effects of the five simulated temperatures. It can retain or downgrade a primary association but can never rescue a failed primary test, establish causality, or turn a null mechanism result into a completeness failure.
preregistration_note: Frozen while the first 500 ps formal trajectory was incomplete and before any formal transport or formal mechanism descriptor existed. A null-model stress test showed that a shared nonlinear temperature curve can confound the primary linear inverse-temperature adjustment, motivating this outcome-blind robustness model.

robustness_model.formula: log transport = occupancy-realization fixed intercept + categorical temperature fixed effect + standardized primary mechanism descriptor
robustness_model.temperature_adjustment: Four indicators represent the five common temperature levels; no linear or Arrhenius functional form is imposed.
robustness_model.weighting: inverse declared trajectory-level log-response measurement variance with residual variance inflation no smaller than one

permutation_test.method: Freedman-Lane Monte Carlo permutation of measurement-standardized reduced-model residuals independently within occupancy realization after categorical temperature adjustment

claim_rule: A primary v1 association is retained only if the categorical-temperature slope has the same sign, its Holm-adjusted permutation p value is no larger than 0.05, its occupancy-cluster bootstrap interval excludes zero, and its sign survives deletion of each occupancy. Otherwise it is reported as temperature-model-sensitive and downgraded to not supported. Robustness support without primary v1 support is not a positive claim.

hard_rules.missing_or_unresolved_primary_input: Block the affected robustness cell and retain the primary result; never silently reduce the family.
hard_rules.temperature_model_sensitive_primary_resu: Downgrade the mechanism association claim without failing computational completeness.
hard_rules.null_primary_family: Retain the complete null result as publishable; the all-primary-supported-associations-survive field is then vacuously true and must not be presented as positive mechanism evidence.
